title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Programme Innovation Lab, in partnership with local actors, corporations, and academic institutions, is fostering locally-led innovations to overcome humanitarian crises. These efforts have benefited over 675,000 people, in Latin America and Africa. The innovations have created disaster-resilient urban communities, provided safe drinking water, improved the well-being and food security of artisanal fishing communities, significantly reduced iron deficiency anaemia in children and women of reproductive age, and strengthened health services and early warning systems to ensure continuous healthcare access during crises. Looking ahead, these innovations will scale up, reaching hundreds of thousands more. By exploring new partnerships, funding opportunities, approaches, and technologies, the lab continues to promote innovations that strengthen resilience and reduce humanitarian needs for those facing poverty and exclusion. Gender equality is mainstreamed throughout all Programme Innovation Lab supported innovations, a flagship example being a mobile app designed to provide support and referral pathways for victims of GBV, who often face significant stigma in Zimbabwe.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 3: People Have Food & Nutrition Security. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: A significant number of initiatives supported by the programme innovation lab will be focused on developing and fostering innovations that will enhance resilience at community and systems level including to extreme weather events and climate change – including climate smart practices for food and nutrition security for food production, harvesting and processing and improved natural resource management. There will also be significant focus on developing innovations to enhance capacities to adapt to climate change through, improved disaster preparedness, early warning and response and early recovery. This will include support to agroecological practices and on how market systems development can promote climate adaptation for food production and sustainable livelihoods. Research and development on a entrepreneurial-associative models for climate resilient livelihoods
